text:
svc-incidents-bot: Paging: SLO alert for streaming API. p99 has spiked above 4s for the last 5m, p95 degraded as well. Multiple streaming clients reporting stalls and truncation. Affected prod region: eu-west-1. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/prod/streaming/slo (alert id: SLO-STREAM-2955) :rotating_light:
elena: acked. oncall here. quick symptoms? are streams disconnecting or just delayed chunks? we need customer impact asap.
amar: seeing a big increase in proxy write latencies and socket send buffers backing up. logs show a pattern of "client_read_slow" and repeated "EPIPE" from proxy-to-client sockets. also seeing sustained TCP retransmits on a subset of client IPs. chunk flush intervals jumped from ~120ms to 2s for some connections.
jun: infra metrics: proxy pool connection utilization in eu-west-1 at 92% for last 20m. Some proxy hosts report high fd usage and epoll wait spikes. there was a minor proxy config roll ~1h ago that touched chunk-flush/coalescing flags. rolling back that change would be quick if we want to test.
elena: ops impact — which customers/clients are seeing disconnects? any high-traffic customers?
ops-bot: Affected customers (sample): [acme-payments, lexical-ai, greenbox]. Top offending client IPs: 35.99.120.3, 18.204.55.60. Error types: stalled stream (chunk delay > 5s), premature EOF on ws, increased reconnect rate.
amar: from runtime traces: cause looks like head-of-line blocking at proxy: when a slow consumer stops reading, TCP buffers fill and proxy stalls the upstream write path. combined with the recent coalescing change, we saw larger buffered chunks and longer pauses while coalesced data waited to fill. effect: tail latency explosions for other clients multiplexed on same proxy.
elena: can we mitigate quickly? suggestions?
jun: immediate mitigations we can do now (low risk):
- roll back the coalescing/flush change on the proxy canary group
- enable per-connection write timeouts to drop very slow consumers after N seconds
- temporarily increase proxy pool (scale up proxy-service) for eu-west-1
- enable aggressive TCP keepalive on streaming sockets
I'll start the scale-up and toggle keepalive.
amar: while jun scales, I'll prepare a rollback of the proxy flag. rollback command: ```
# rollback flag on staging canary then prod
kubectl set env deployment/proxy -n streaming PROXY_CHUNK_COALESCE=false --record
kubectl rollout restart deployment/proxy -n streaming
```
elena: try the rollback on a single canary host first, monitor p95/p99. if that helps, we can roll across region. canary ID? jun?
jun: canary rolling now on proxy-ix-03. also bumped replicas +2: ```
kubectl scale deployment/proxy -n streaming --replicas=12
```
(small note: autoscaler still intact, this is manual for immediate headroom)
mar: typo — I'm amar, not mar :)
elena: thanks. next — do we want to temporarily add a fast path that rejects very slow consumers (server-side backpressure blocklist)?
amar: yes, we have an existing "slow-consumer" gate. enabling with a short TTL will drop the worst offenders quickly. command: ```
# enable quick eviction for slow consumers > 6s
curl -XPOST http://controlplane.internal/flags -d '{"slow_consumer_evict_threshold_ms":6000}'
```
jun: flag enabled on controlplane. monitoring now.
ops-bot: Controlplane accepted flag change. eviction active.
elena: any sign of immediate change in SLOs?
amar: initial numbers 2m after mitigations: p95 down from 1.1s -> 0.85s, p99 from 4.2s -> 1.9s. number of stalled streams (>5s) dropped by ~78%. still seeing a small tail spike on a couple canary proxies.
elena: good. can we identify if this was caused primarily by client behavior or our proxy change?
amar: root cause is mixed: a subset of clients had pathological slow consumption (likely client-side GC pauses or network), but our recent change to coalesce chunks made the proxy buffer more and therefore exacerbated head-of-line effects. without coalescing, smaller writes flush more frequently which reduces stall propagation.
jun: infra note: several proxy hosts hit high epoll backlog after the canary flag. CPU was fine but syscall wait increased. rolling rollback across the region now after canary success.
elena: roll it carefully. prioritize hosts with most active streaming connections. also create a list of customer-facing incidents for the affected customers.
ops-bot: new incident ticket created: INC-2026-2955. Customers notified: acme-payments (via account rep), lexical-ai (email), greenbox (support ticket).
amar: follow-up actions I propose (postmortem TODOs):
- revert coalescing change in stable branch until we have per-connection flow-control improvements
- add per-connection tail-sampling logs and record slow-consumer stack traces if available
- add metrics for coalesced-chunk-size and per-client buffer occupancy
- implement adaptive chunk-flush that flushes more frequently to slow readers
- add a safety circuit that drops single connection that blocks > X ms instead of stalling all others
elena: agree. I'll own the incident doc and postmortem. I'll also hand off to the next oncall for monitoring.
maya: taking over oncall at +1. I'll watch the SLO dashboard for the next 2 hours and coordinate customer comms.
elena: handover notes: mitigations applied: scale proxies +2, enabled slow-consumer eviction, rolled back PROXY_CHUNK_COALESCE on canary then region. Immediate impact: p99 reduced to ~1.8s and stalled streams dropped 78%. Next steps: postmortem, metric additions, conservative rollback in stable branch.
amar: one more note — we saw increased keepalive timeouts on long-running mobile clients. Recommend default keepalive shorten from 120s -> 30s for streaming sockets.
jun: putting a followup task in infra backlog and will attach diffs for the rollback.
elena: closing incident channel for active triage. Will update INC-2026-2955 with timeline and actions. thanks everyone :clap:
